_about: Straight-line distance (km) from the last seen point to where people of each category were found, as percentiles. Numbers are facts quoted from the sources with citation; the source documents themselves are not redistributed. 'quality' says how much to trust the table. Percentiles a source does not give are interpolated by the code between the given points (0 km at 0 %).
terrain_rule: ISRID convention: 'mountain' when the elevation range within 5 km of the point exceeds 305 m (1000 ft), else 'flat'; 'urban' when built-up covers over half of the 1 km around the point; 'dry' when bare/sparse vegetation covers over 30 % of the 5 km around the point.

sources.uk2011: Perkins, Roberts, Feeney (2011) The UK Missing Person Behaviour Study, Centre for Search Research, https://tcsr.org.uk/media/kushuk1a/uk-missing-person-behaviour-study-2011.pdf
sources.koester2008: Koester (2008) Lost Person Behavior, dementia sample chapter p.164, https://www.dbs-sar.com/LPB/Dementia.pdf
sources.koester2025: Koester (2025) LPB updates, ICAR 2025 slides, slide 15 (miles converted to km), https://www.alpine-rescue.org/system/production/article/documents/file/005/312/a4507c99bbf7f6ade0b44cd1068b2354b42ae1dd3748ad1612445944f372f92c/20251009-1130-ICAR_2025_LPB_Koester.pdf
sources.sava2015: Sava, Twardy, Koester, Sonwalkar (2015) Transactions in GIS, Table 1, reproducing Koester 2008 hiker figures (in miles; converted), http://geoinf.psu.edu/publications/2015_TransGIS_Search_Sava.pdf
sources.twardy2006: Twardy, Koester, Gatt (2006) Missing person behaviour: an Australian study, Tables 2.2 and 2.8, https://esf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/RobertGatt2002VicPol.pdf
sources.asrc2007: ASRC Operations Manual draft (2007) lost person behavior table; units not stated, read as miles and converted, 'max' column not 95 %, https://www.archive.asrc.net/ASRC-Operations/ASRC-Operations-Manual/2007-03-12-ASRC-OpsMan-Lost-Person-Behavior-draft.pdf
sources.d4h: D4H blog quoting Koester 2008 for child 1-3 (secondhand), https://www.d4h.com/blog/dr-robert-koesters-lost-person-behavior-and-how-to-contribute-to-isrid
sources.grampian2007: Gibb, Woolnough (2007) Missing persons: understanding, planning, responding (Grampian Police), mostly urban police data, https://www.missingpersons.gov.au/sites/default/files/PDF%20-%20Publications/Research/International/Missing%20Persons%20Understanding%20Planning%20Respondi.pdf

elderly.quality: 'normal' elderly; units assumed miles; 'max' used as 99 %

hunter_forager.quality: hunters; used for foragers and shepherds too (no open table); units assumed miles; 'max' used as 99 %

intellectual_disability.quality: Virginia; used for autism too (no open autism table)
